title: Early Planet Formation in Embedded Disks (eDisk). XXII. Keplerian Disk, Disk Structures, and Jets/Outflows in the Class 0 Protostar IRAS 04166+2706
question: What are the dust disk structure, gas kinematics (Keplerian rotation and protostellar mass) and jet/outflow properties of the Class 0 protostar IRAS 04166+2706 at 1.3 mm with eDisk?

data.arrays: 12-m array, two configurations: C43-8 (long baseline) and C43-5 (short baseline)
data.angular_resolution: ~0.05" (~8 au) for continuum; ~0.16" (~25 au) for lines
data.sensitivity: Continuum rms 23 uJy/beam; line rms 0.7-3.1 mJy/beam (Table 1)

evidence.quote: More recently, (cite: Krolikowski+etal_2021) used the new data of Gaia EDR3 and calculated the distance of the region to be 155.94 pc.

what.value: Bolometric luminosity 0.41 Lsun and bolometric temperature 54 K (Class 0 classification)

evidence.quote: the eDisk collaboration estimated the bolometric luminosity and temperature of the source to be 0.41 L$_\odot$ and 54 K respectively

what.value: Dust mass opacity kappa(1.3 mm) = 2.3 cm^2 per g

evidence.quote: We adopt the dust opacity of $\kappa_{1.3\,mm}$=2.3 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ (cite: Beckwith+etal_1990)

what.value: Dust temperature of 20 K, median of Taurus disks

evidence.quote: assume a dust temperature of 20 K which is the median value of dust temperatures of disks in the Taurus star-forming region as derived by (cite: Andrews+etal_2005)

what.value: Luminosity-based dust temperature relation for Class 0/I disks (gives ~34 K here)

evidence.quote: (cite: Tobin+etal_2020) introduced a more realistic method to estimate the dust temperature of Class 0/I objects based on the source luminosity as

what.value: IRAM PdBI 1.3 mm flux density of 59 +/- 2 mJy

evidence.quote: than the value of $59\pm2$ mJy by IRAM PdBI observations at 1.3 mm (cite: Santiago+etal_2009)

what.value: Disk mass 0.027 Msun from RADMC-3D modeling and MCMC SED fit

evidence.quote: (0.027 M$_\odot$) from RADMC-3D modeling and MCMC fit using a wide range SED set data including CARMA mm data (cite: Sheehan+Eisner_2017)

what.value: Planet formation efficiency of order 15% for Class 0 disks

evidence.loc: 5.1 Brightness asymmetry, dust mass in the disk, and disk stability
evidence.quote: the planet formation efficiency is of the order of $15\%$ assuming that the planet starts to form in the Class 0 disk

recipe.goal: Calibrate, self-calibrate and image the eDisk data
recipe.method: Manual pipeline run for semi-pass EBs; per-EB imaging and shift to a common phase center from imfit; visibility-amplitude scale factors between EBs; two-pass phase and amplitude self-calibration on short baseline then combined data; imaging with tclean
key_parameters: robust = 0.0 for continuum, robust = 2.0 for lines; robust = 2.0 plus 1000 klambda uv taper for extended dust emission

recipe.goal: Fit the continuum disk geometry and flux
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit with imfit to the robust = 0.0 image; inclination from cos^-1 of minor/major axis ratio
key_parameters: Fit on robust = 0.0 image without uv tapering

recipe.method: Optically thin, isothermal dust mass equation M_d = S_nu d^2 / (kappa_nu B_nu(T_d)) with S_nu = 70.8 mJy, d = 156 pc, nu = 225 GHz; total mass with gas-to-dust ratio of 100
key_parameters: kappa(1.3 mm) = 2.3 cm^2 per g; T_d = 20 K (Taurus median) or ~34 K from T_d = 43 (L_bol/Lsun)^0.25 with L_bol = 0.41 Lsun
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio of 100; optically thin emission (otherwise mass is a lower limit)

recipe.goal: Search the continuum disk for rings/gaps via radial profile
recipe.method: Deproject the image, azimuthally average in 0.01" annuli, fit two Gaussian functions to the radial profile, then fit Gaussian functions to the residual rings
key_parameters: Deprojection with PA = 121.5 deg and inclination = 47 deg from the 2D Gaussian fit

recipe.goal: Fit edge and ridge of 13CO and C18O PV diagrams
recipe.method: PV diagrams along the disk major axis (PA 122 deg) within one beam width; edge and ridge extracted with pvanalysis of SLAM and fitted with a power law V_rot = v_b (r/r_b)^-p
key_parameters: Ridge threshold 6 sigma for 13CO and 3 sigma for C18O; edge threshold not stated

recipe.goal: Derive protostellar mass limits from Keplerian motion
recipe.method: Keplerian rotation v = sqrt(G M / r) at inclination 47 deg applied to edge and ridge results; lowest and highest values adopted as lower and upper mass limits
assumptions: Gas in the small region is in Keplerian motion; ridge fitting underestimates and edge fitting overestimates the mass

recipe.goal: Map jets/outflows and date the ejection events
recipe.method: Moment 0/1 maps of 12CO and SiO in velocity bins, PV diagrams along the jet axis (PA 32 deg), and knot-distance/velocity timescales
key_parameters: SiO moments computed in -70 to 70 km/s with 3 sigma threshold
Average jet velocity 40 km/s within 11 arcsec radius; inclination 47 deg for the ejection period
assumptions: Distance 156 pc and i = 47 deg used to convert projected distance and velocity to the ejection period

recipe.method: Integrated flux ratio between northeastern and southwestern hemispheres; intensity profiles along major and minor axes; compared qualitatively with RADMC-3D synthetic images of Takakuwa et al.

recipe.goal: Assess disk gravitational stability with Toomre Q
recipe.method: Q = c_s Omega / (pi G Sigma) = 2 (M_star / M_disk)(H/R) with R = 22 au, M_star = 0.15-0.39 Msun, M_disk = 0.015 and 0.008 Msun
assumptions: Disk is geometrically thin; instability for Q < 1-1.5

score_reason: Observations, software versions and key fit parameters are given and results are numeric, but most reduction details are deferred to the eDisk overview paper and self-calibration, imaging and fit settings are missing.
rediscovery_reason: eDisk is an ALMA Large Program with a project code and the continuum Gaussian fit, dust mass and PV-fit stellar mass are numeric and redoable, though the two-pass self-calibration needs the eDisk scripts and the data archive status is not stated in the paper.
